name: MetaCapabilities deny widening and separate structural powers

input.source_text: class A meta deny method_set { public fun m() -> Symbol { :live } } class B meta deny method_body { } class C meta deny method_set { } class D extends C { } module Q { public fun run() -> Object { let before = A.active_revision; let set_denied = try { A.define_method(:x) { 1 } } catch e { e }; let body_allows_set = try { B.define_method(:x) { 1 } } catch e { e }; let inherited = try { D.define_method(:x) { 1 } } catch e { e }; [set_denied, body_allows_set, inherited, D.denied_capabilities, before, A.active_revision, A.new().m()] } } Q.run()

applicability.reason: Supported for the operation-level half, and a real defect was fixed to get here. C080 makes MetaCapabilities orthogonal and C081's matrix separates method_set from method_body: denying the latter leaves `define_method` allowed, denying the former refuses it, and the refusal is atomic - the revision is unchanged and the declared member still answers. C152's inherited deny carries to a subclass. The defect: C081 makes the method-slot operation `static only for origin`, but a Class DECLARING its own members was checked against its own deny, so `class A meta deny method_set { public fun m() { ... } }` failed at its own declaration and a Class could deny the capability only by declaring nothing. That is why META-V360's fixture uses an empty body. The origin declaration is no longer checked.
